at_rest.evidence: apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-host.tf, resource "hcloud_volume" "inngest_redis" — the block carries NO format attribute and a `lifecycle` stanza that ignores changes to one. CORRECTED 2026-09-03 (#7695): this field previously cited "the `format = \"ext4\"` attribute, retained under `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [format] }`", which stopped being true in the same change that dropped the attribute — the citation survived the edit it described. The attribute was removed because `ignore_changes` suppresses diffs and never creates, so with it declared the recut's replacement volume would have been created ext4 and the one-shot empty-store window spent on an unencrypted store; the lifecycle stanza is retained because it is what keeps the EXISTING volume's plan a no-op. The live device is plaintext ext4 from its 2026-07-07 creation, which is a fact about the disk rather than about the config — and that is why this row is anchored on the resource rather than on any attribute of it. CONTENT-ANCHORED, not line-numbered (cq-cite-content-anchor-not-line-number). The citation this replaces named a line number in the same file; the resource had since moved 139 lines down it, so the record pointed at unrelated bytes. The literal is not repeated here because AC B3 greps this file for that shape, and a record that documents the forbidden form cannot also assert its absence.
at_rest.does_not_defend: a seized/snapshot disk exposes the Inngest queue + run-state AOF, i.e. in-flight job payloads (user prompts and agent output)
at_rest.live_verification: unavailable:the Hetzner API is blind to guest-side LUKS. CORRECTED 2026-09-03 (#7695): a posture probe now EXISTS — SOLEUR_INNGEST_SERVER_PROBE emits data_mount_src (the findmnt source of /mnt/data) at probe_schema=3, so the mount substrate is readable off-box without SSH. It still cannot verify THIS row, because the row asserts PLAINTEXT and the probe reports the by-id device either way; it becomes the live verification the moment mechanism flips to luks and the expected source becomes /dev/mapper/inngest-redis. Tracked #6894.

exception.justification: highest-sensitivity plaintext store. REASSESSED 2026-09-03 (#7695): the LUKS apparatus now EXISTS and has merged — a five-arm blkid discriminator in cloud-init-inngest.yml, a boot-reopen unit, and a passphrase minted at merge (inngest-redis-luks.tf). It is INERT: the device becomes crypto_LUKS only when the gated apply_target=inngest-volume-recut dispatch destroys and recreates the volume raw, and two guards refuse that dispatch unless the host is measured dark and the store measured empty (ADR-199). The store is therefore still plaintext and this exception still holds; what changed is that the remaining work is one gated dispatch rather than an unbuilt mechanism.
exception.expires_on_not_extended: The expiry below is DELIBERATELY unchanged. Re-dating an at-rest exception forward is buying more plaintext time, and nothing measured here justifies that: the apparatus being built does not encrypt anything. The assessment date above is what moved.
exception.reevaluate_when: the inngest-volume-recut dispatch completes AND a boot is observed reaching SOLEUR_INNGEST_LUKS_STAGE stage=verify with data_mount_src=/dev/mapper/inngest-redis. Flip mechanism to luks in that follow-up commit, never before — asserting encryption over an unbounded window while the volume is still ext4 would be a false at-rest claim about user prompts and agent output.

exception.justification: It mirrors the PROD plaintext store BY DESIGN. Making the rehearsal volume LUKS while hcloud_volume.git_data is plaintext would rehearse a boot that does not exist — the rung-2 rehearsal's entire value is that it boots what production would boot, so its dual-volume shape has to match production's, including the part that is currently unencrypted.
exception.reevaluate_when: hcloud_volume.git_data becomes the LUKS volume (the GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED cutover) — at which point this mirror must move with it, or the rehearsal stops rehearsing production

at_rest.evidence: Cloudflare Pages stores deployment assets on Cloudflare-managed infrastructure encrypted at rest; Cloudflare holds an AICPA SOC 2 Type II attestation (Security/Confidentiality/Availability) per the Cloudflare Trust Hub - the report is NDA-gated, the attestation's existence and scope are public. connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> zot registry over the CF Tunnel (registry.<base> -> tcp://10.0.1.30:5000)

in_transit.tls: runner<->CF edge and CF edge<->origin connector: TLS 1.2+ (raw TCP over WebSocket). origin connector<->10.0.1.30:5000: PLAIN HTTP on the Hetzner private network, by design.
in_transit.does_not_defend: a passive on-net attacker on 10.0.1.0/24 could read image bytes on the final leg; integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not TLS. Also does not defend a leaked CF Access service token or a leaked zot pull credential.

exception.justification: the same private-network-only exception already recorded for 'web hosts -> zot registry' - the final leg is plain HTTP inside the Hetzner private network; image bytes are our own OCI layers and integrity is cosign-digest-pinned. Folded in here rather than deferred because #7278 adds the fifth CI caller to this leg.
exception.reevaluate_when: the registry link gains TLS, or the store is exposed beyond the private network
